label: Rates for 2026 to 2027
title: Capital gains tax in 2026 to 2027: rates, the £3,000 allowance and the new 18% BADR rate
summary: Most gains are taxed at 18% or 24%, the annual exempt amount stays at £3,000, and Business Asset Disposal Relief now gives 18%.
body:
If you sell a property that is not your main home, shares, crypto or a business this tax year, here is how the gain is taxed.

The rates

  • Gains within your remaining basic rate band are taxed at 18%.
  • Gains above it are taxed at 24%. This applies to residential property and other assets alike.
  • The annual exempt amount is £3,000 for individuals.
  • Gains qualifying for Business Asset Disposal Relief or Investors' Relief are taxed at 18% from 6 April 2026, up from 14% in 2025 to 2026.

To find which rate applies, add the taxable gain to your taxable income. The basic rate band for 2026 to 2027 is £37,700.

An example

A higher rate taxpayer sells shares with a gain of £20,000. After the £3,000 allowance, £17,000 is taxable at 24%, so the tax is £4,080.

The BADR change

Business owners selling a trading business or qualifying shares used to pay 10% under this relief, then 14% in 2025 to 2026. From 6 April 2026 it is 18%. That is now the same as the basic rate on other gains, but for higher rate taxpayers it is still 6 points less than 24%. The £1 million lifetime limit still applies.

What I would do

  • Sold a UK residential property? Report and pay within 60 days of completion.
  • Keep purchase and sale costs and improvement receipts. They reduce the gain.
  • Married couples and civil partners can transfer assets between them without tax, which may allow both allowances and basic rate bands to be used. Get advice before the sale, not after.
